claims.text: Elevated-temperature anomalies in HfNbTaTiZr stress–strain behavior, thermal expansion, and elastic properties arise from thermally activated local chemical segregation.
Thermally activated local chemical segregation triggers short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal exposure triggers dynamic recovery processes that contribute to the elevated-temperature responses of HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is a homogenized, disordered solid solution at room temperature.
Using comparable strain rates and thermal histories isolates the effects of temperature on microstructural evolution.
Increasing temperature induces local chemical segregation and emergent short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Elevated temperature promotes dynamic recovery through processes including dislocation climb and vacancy migration.
Above a critical temperature, atomic mobility becomes sufficient to induce local compositional fluctuations.
Localized changes in chemical order alter lattice parameters and thereby affect thermal expansion.
Localized changes in chemical order modify dislocation interactions and thereby affect stress–strain and elastic responses.
Local chemical ordering and dynamic recovery produce nonlinear changes in mechanical properties relative to the disordered baseline state.
Above approximately 600°C, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a nonlinear increase in thermal expansion relative to room-temperature and low-temperature baselines.
Above approximately 600°C, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit decreased yield strength relative to room-temperature and low-temperature baselines.
Above approximately 600°C, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit altered elastic moduli relative to room-temperature and low-temperature baselines.
The predicted changes above approximately 600°C indicate the onset of local ordering and dynamic recovery.
The predicted effects should be measurable from approximately 600°C to 1000°C.
Below approximately 600°C, atomic mobility is insufficient to drive the predicted local ordering.
